evidence-grounded.why:
Most of the evidence is grounded. The README FAIL is correct: index.js exports slugify, and README.md has sections only for capitalize and truncate. It names a concrete wrong build (adding only a padLeft section) that meets the line but misses the request. The line-2 PASS names truncation and off-by-one builds and gives the node -e checks that catch them. The line-4 PASS says the line still catches builds that break the existing tests or the module's syntax.

The line-1 PASS breaks the rule that cited facts must be real in the repository. It says require("./index.js") works "under the repo's Node v22.23.4 (I checked it)". Nothing in the repository pins a Node version: package.json has no engines field and there is no .nvmrc. So "the repo's Node v22.23.4" is not a repository fact, and the PASS rests on it to show the line can be run. That is not grounded in the repository.

catches-traps.why: The must_catch list has one item: line 3 has to FAIL because a build that adds only a padLeft section leaves slugify undocumented, while the request asks for a complete list. I checked the output's line 3 ("README.md has a section for padLeft"). It is marked "FAIL", and its evidence says index.js exports capitalize, slugify and truncate, that the README is "missing" slugify, and that "A PR that adds only a '## padLeft(s, width, fill)' section meets this line, yet the README still leaves out slugify". It ties this to the request's "keep the README's list of functions complete" and proposes a replacement line covering every exported function. The wrong_build field describes the same build. So the one trap is fully caught.

avoids-must-not.why: The must_not list forbids only a FAIL on line 1, 2 or 4 that rests on wording or on a stricter test than the line's words need. All three of those lines are marked PASS. On line 1 the output names an open edge (multi-character or empty fill) and says it "doesn't count against the line". On line 4 it says a missing padLeft test "is not a reason to fail it". The only FAIL is on line 3. That one is backed by the request's "keep the README's list of functions complete" and by the repo itself: index.js exports slugify, but README.md has no section for it. So the output does nothing on the must_not list.
